claim_scope: Dickinson & Pauling (1923) first-page EXCERPT: the mineral molybdenite, MoS2, occurs in hexagonal crystals with basal cleavage, studied by X-ray. Primary-scientific support (excerpt-scoped) for the molybdenite / MoS2 / HEXAGONAL identity underpinning the (later-named) 2H structure. Does NOT establish the modern '2H' label.

locator.system: J. Am. Chem. Soc. 45, 1466-1471 (1923), first-page excerpt image
locator.verbatim: The mineral molybdenite, MoS2, is described as occurring in hexagonal crystals with a very complete basal cleavage. A study of its crystal structure has been carried out using X-ray spectral photographs and Laue photographs treated as previously described.

observations_full_article_pp_1466_1471: p. 1466 (PDF p. 2): quotation above present; density 4.92 g/cc (the OCR text layer misreads it as 1.02); d0001 = 6.15 Å for the smaller trial unit, axial ratio 1.95
p. 1467 (PDF p. 3): adopted unit d0001 = 12.30 Å, axial ratio 3.90, containing 2 MoS2
p. 1470 (PDF p. 6): each Mo surrounded by six S at the corners of a triangular prism, altitude 3.17 ± 0.10, edge 3.15 ± 0.02; Mo–S 2.41 ± 0.06 Å; Fig. 2 labels the cell 3.15 Å by 12.30 Å
the label '2H' does not occur in the article
